model: Sum-of-parts holdco: Bajaj Finance stake as FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), insurance stakes and holdco items in the equity bridge

inputs.base_revenue_note: BFS's 51.2% economic share of Bajaj Finance FY2026 (year to 31 Mar 2026) consolidated net interest income of INR 439,399m (stockanalysis.com 'Revenue', which ties to BFL's reported NII: FY2024 31,669 cr). This is the revenue base of the DCF'd STREAM, not BFS consolidated total income (INR 1,500,053m FY2026) -- the insurers are valued in the equity bridge, not in the flows.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 1,601m basic on issue at 30 Sep 2026 (stockanalysis.com) plus ~11m of unexercised ESOP dilution (FY2025 AR diluted 1,611.65m vs basic 1,595.49m = 16.2m, of which ~5.5m since exercised). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed inside subsidiary PAT.
inputs.net_debt_note: Bajaj Finserv standalone carries no borrowings (FY2025 AR standalone balance sheet: no debt securities or borrowings; cash 18.0 cr, bank balances 0.9 cr; surplus held as investments). Consolidated debt of INR 3.54tn (FY2025) is Bajaj Finance/BHFL lending funding and is NOT net debt -- it is the operating liability of the lender whose equity flows are being valued. Standalone surplus funds are carried as an equity-bridge item instead of cash.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2026 FCFE of the stream: Bajaj Finance attributable PAT 19,017 cr less equity retained to fund book growth (attributable equity 116,986 cr at Mar-2026 vs 98,937 cr at Mar-2025 = 18,049 cr) = 968 cr x 51.2% = 496 cr = INR 4,957m. BFS's consolidated reported FCF (INR -639,768m FY2025, Metrics.csv) is structurally negative because loan-book growth runs through operating cash flow; it is not an owner-earnings measure for a lender and is deliberately not used.
inputs.sbc_source: Consolidated SBC INR 5,456m FY2025 (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp; mostly Bajaj Finance ESOPs) is already expensed inside subsidiary PAT under Ind AS 102, and the stream is PAT-based, so it is not deducted a second time (charge-once rule). Explicit SBC rows kept at 0%. House and street therefore coincide; band_position is null by construction.
inputs.price_note: NSE regular close Friday 6 Nov 2026 (valuation date 8 Nov is a Saturday). Not an after-hours print.
inputs.balance_sheet_note: Bajaj Finance attributable equity INR 1,263,653m and 6,223m shares at 30 Sep 2026 (stockanalysis.com, Q2 FY2027). BFS standalone surplus funds INR 34,840m at 30 Sep 2025 (H1 FY2026 investor deck, the latest filing in the corpus) less the Jan-2026 outlay for the 1.01% insurer stakes (~INR 9,390m) = INR 25,450m. BAGIC net worth 13,433 cr and BALIC embedded value 25,357 cr are 30 Sep 2025. The FY2026 annual report and H1 FY2027 results are NOT yet in Extracted/ -- refresh when they are.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single INR cost of equity 12.5% across all scenarios (risk charged once, via scenario weights and the scenario-specific holdco discount). Built in the flows' own currency: India 10-year G-sec ~6.5% + beta ~0.9 x India total equity risk premium ~6.5-7.0% (mature-market ~4.3% plus country premium) = ~12.3-12.6%. Identical to the HDB/IBN India-bank builds in this folder so the Indian financials are comparable. Terminal growth 5.5/6.0/6.5% (bear/base/bull) in INR against ~9-10% nominal GDP -- a notch below the HDB/IBN base of 6.5% because of the extra holdco layer.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: the stream is a PAT-based FCFE of Bajaj Finance (lease costs sit inside its operating expenses) and no lease liabilities enter the bridge. Charged once, inside the flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows. The stream is BFS's 51.2% attributable share of Bajaj Finance (BFS held 51.32% at 30 Sep 2025 per the H1 FY2026 deck; BFL's share count has since crept +0.2% on ESOPs, so 51.2%). Bajaj Housing Finance's 11.3% minority is folded into the leakage rate (cash_tax_rate_path). Insurance stakes are taken at 75.01% of 100% value in the bridge. No separate NCI stock deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Sum-of-the-parts for a diversified financial holding company, routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md (insurer/holdco row + 'straddles two rows -> value the parts and sum'; also the 'sum-of-parts with an embedded lender' case in the agent contract). A consolidated owner-FCF DCF is meaningless here: consolidated FCF is -INR 640bn because loan growth runs through OCF, and consolidated PAT is after a ~49% minority. PARTS: (1) Bajaj Finance 51.2% -- the DCF'd stream (about 75-80% of value). Revenue = BFS's share of BFL net interest income; ebitda_margin_path = PBT/NII (FY2026 ~58%, PBT 25,526 cr on NII 43,940 cr); da, sbc, working capital = 0; capex_pct_path = EQUITY RETENTION required to fund book growth = ER_t - ER_(t-1)/(1+g_t), where ER is attributable equity / NII (2.66x at Mar-2026, CRAR 21.2%; base glides to 2.20x i.e. CRAR drifting toward ~17.5% as excess capital is levered, bear holds ~2.60x, bull to 2.00x). FCF therefore = FCFE = attributable PAT less retention, and FY0 NOPAT ties to attributable PAT (51.2% x 19,017 cr = 9,737 cr before the holdco discount). cash_tax_rate_path is the tax + minority leakage rate: BFL effective tax ~24% + BHFL minority ~1.5% = 25.5% in every scenario (risk is NOT charged here). (2) Bajaj General Insurance 75.01% and (3) Bajaj Life Insurance 75.01% -- equity bridge at the 17-Mar-2025 Allianz SPA values (26% of BAGIC for 13,780 cr => 53,000 cr for 100%, 28.9x FY2025 PAT 1,832 cr, 3.9x Sep-2025 net worth 13,433 cr; 26% of BALIC for 10,400 cr => 40,000 cr for 100%, 1.58x Sep-2025 embedded value 25,357 cr, vs listed life peers at 1.5-2.7x EV), (the bridge cannot vary by scenario; +/-20% on the insurer anchors is ~+/-INR 69/share after the holdco discount). BFS buys only 1.01% of each insurer (to 75.01%); the other 24.99% goes to promoter-group entities (FY2025 AR p.5137-5160), so the Analysis JSON's 'toward 100%' refers to the Bajaj GROUP, not BFS. (4) Emerging businesses at book/AUM: Bajaj Finserv Health 100% (net worth 455 cr), Bajaj Finserv Direct 80.1% (383 cr NW => 307 cr), Bajaj Finserv AMC 100% at ~1.5% of 28,814 cr AUM (~430 cr; NW ~117 cr), windfarm ~50 cr; total ~1,240 cr. (5) Standalone surplus funds 2,545 cr (see balance_sheet_note). (6) Capitalised holdco leakage: standalone other expenses 238 cr/yr (FY2025 AR Table 11) capitalised at 12.5%-4.5% => ~2,975 cr, plus incubation losses ~530 cr/yr (Health -130, Direct -180, AMC -220 run-rate, Q2 FY2026) tapering to zero over five years => ~1,070 cr PV; total -4,045 cr. HOLDCO DISCOUNT: BFS trades at a 27.8% discount to its parts marked at market (BFL stake 3,46,576 cr at INR 1,087.75 + insurers 69,759 cr + other ~-260 cr = INR 2,581/share vs price 1,864.7); the model carries a single bridge item of 20% of the BASE-case look-through value of the BFL stake and insurers (sell-side convention for BFS is 15-25% on the BFL stake); because it is a fixed INR amount it is ~30% of the bear case's own look-through value and ~15% of the bull's -- the widening-in-stress, narrowing-in-strength pattern intended. An earlier draft carried the discount inside cash_tax_rate_path; that was wrong because it haircut NOPAT but not the equity retention, so FCFE came out as 0.8xPAT - retention instead of 0.8x(PAT - retention). ANCHOR VINTAGE: price 6 Nov 2026; BFL equity/shares 30 Sep 2026; BFS standalone and insurer anchors 30 Sep 2025 (latest filing in corpus) -- refresh when the FY2026 AR and H1 FY2027 deck are extracted. DATA CHECK: Bajaj Finance Q3 FY2026 (Dec-2025) revenue in the stockanalysis.com quarterly table (102,504m) looks like a source glitch; only annual and TTM figures were used.

equity_bridge.item: Bajaj General Insurance (ex-BAGIC) 75.01% stake at Allianz SPA value: 100% = 53,000 cr (26% sold for 13,780 cr, 17 Mar 2025)
equity_bridge.note: 28.9x FY2025 PAT 1,832 cr; 3.9x net worth 13,433 cr at 30 Sep 2025; solvency 339%; COR 102.3% Q2 FY2026. Held at the Mar-2025 deal price despite ~10%/yr profit growth since, offsetting the loss of Allianz's reinsurance/technical support.

equity_bridge.item: Bajaj Life Insurance (ex-BALIC) 75.01% stake at Allianz SPA value: 100% = 40,000 cr (26% sold for 10,400 cr, 17 Mar 2025)
equity_bridge.note: 1.58x embedded value 25,357 cr at 30 Sep 2025 (23,805 cr at FY2025; RoEV 12.3%); VNB 1,152 cr FY2025, 1,315 cr rolling to Sep-2025; NBM 17.1% Q2 FY2026; solvency 346%. Listed peers 1.5-2.7x EV.

equity_bridge.item: Holdco discount: 20% of the base-case look-through value of the Bajaj Finance stake (stream EV 1,879,158m, undiscounted) and the two insurance stakes (697,593m)
equity_bridge.note: Fixed INR amount so it lives in the bridge (which cannot vary by scenario); as a share of each scenario's own look-through value it is ~30% bear / 20% base / ~15% bull. Not applied to surplus cash or the emerging businesses. Market-implied discount to parts-at-market was 27.8% on 6 Nov 2026.

equity_bridge.item: Emerging businesses at book / AUM: Bajaj Finserv Health 100% (NW 455 cr), Bajaj Finserv Direct 80.1% (NW 383 cr => 307 cr), Bajaj Finserv AMC 100% (~1.5% of AUM 28,814 cr => ~430 cr), windfarm (~50 cr)
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 deck pp.6-9 (30 Sep 2025). All still loss-making except the windfarm; their forward losses are charged in the leakage item below.

equity_bridge.item: Standalone surplus funds 3,484 cr at 30 Sep 2025 less Jan-2026 outlay of ~939 cr for the 1.01% insurer stakes (1.01/26 x 24,180 cr)
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 deck p.4 'Surplus Funds (Standalone)'. Standalone has no borrowings. Its investment income is excluded from the stream, so the asset belongs in the bridge (matching-asset rule).

equity_bridge.item: Capitalised holdco costs and incubation losses: standalone other expenses 238 cr/yr at (12.5% - 4.5%) => -2,975 cr; emerging-business losses ~530 cr/yr tapering to zero over five years => -1,070 cr PV
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 AR Table 11 (standalone other expenses 238 cr); Q2 FY2026 PAT: Health -32 cr, Direct -45 cr, AMC -55.7 cr per quarter.

historical_growth.notes: CAGRs from Metrics.csv consolidated series, FY2022->FY2025 (3yr) and FY2020->FY2025 (5yr), INR millions, Ind AS throughout. Revenue = consolidated total income (insurance gross premiums + lending income); EPS and net income are attributable to owners on the post-Sep-2022 split+bonus share basis. FCF CAGRs are not meaningful: consolidated FCF is negative in every year but FY2021 because Bajaj Finance's loan-book growth runs through operating cash flow, so attributable net income CAGRs are reported instead. Equity 5yr CAGR 18.3% is within 30% of revenue (19.7%) and EPS (21.3%), so no divergence warning. The base case starts Bajaj Finance NII growth at 24% (H1 FY2027 actual +26% revenue, +27% PAT) and tapers to 8% by FY2036 -- a deliberate deceleration below every historical CAGR.

base.growth_note: Bajaj Finance NII growth: FY2027 24% (H1 FY2027 revenue +26%, PAT +27%; FY2026 AUM guidance was 22-23% after the MSME pullback), then a straight taper to 8% by FY2036.
base.ebitda_margin_note: PBT / NII. FY2026 actual ~58.1% (PBT 25,526 cr on NII 43,940 cr); 58.0% in FY2027 as credit costs (1.85-1.95% guided, improving in FY2027) offset by opex leverage, then 58.5% flat.
base.capex_note: Equity retention to fund growth = ER_t - ER_(t-1)/(1+g_t) with ER (attributable equity / NII) 2.66 at FY2026 gliding 2.55, 2.50, 2.46, 2.42, 2.38, 2.34, 2.30, 2.27, 2.23, 2.20 (CRAR 21.2% drifting toward ~17.5%). FY2036 retention 13.5% vs steady-state 2.20 x 6%/1.06 = 12.5% -- matured, slightly conservative.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: Tax + minority leakage: Bajaj Finance effective tax ~24% (FY2025: 1 - 16,779/22,080) + Bajaj Housing Finance's 11.3% minority ~1.5% of PAT = 25.5%. FY2027 NOPAT therefore equals 51.2% of BFL attributable PAT (12,054 cr on the base path). The holdco discount is NOT in this rate; it is an explicit equity-bridge item.

bull.growth_note: BFL sustains its long-range 25-27% AUM ambition for three years as credit costs normalise, tapering to 9%.
bull.cash_tax_rate_note: Tax + minority leakage: Bajaj Finance effective tax ~24% (FY2025: 1 - 16,779/22,080) + Bajaj Housing Finance's 11.3% minority ~1.5% of PAT = 25.5%. FY2027 NOPAT therefore equals 51.2% of BFL attributable PAT (12,054 cr on the base path). The holdco discount is NOT in this rate; it is an explicit equity-bridge item.

bear.growth_note: Unsecured retail/MSME credit cycle turns (GNPA was 1.24% in Q2 FY2026, a 10-quarter high) and RBI tightens again: growth halves to 15% in FY2027 and settles at 5-8%.
bear.ebitda_margin_note: Credit costs 2.5%+ compress PBT/NII to 52% in FY2028-29, recovering only to 54%.
bear.capex_note: No capital release: ER 2.62 then 2.60 flat (stress keeps CRAR ~21%); FY2036 retention at steady state 2.60 x 5.5%/1.055 = 13.6%.
bear.cash_tax_rate_note: Tax + minority leakage: Bajaj Finance effective tax ~24% (FY2025: 1 - 16,779/22,080) + Bajaj Housing Finance's 11.3% minority ~1.5% of PAT = 25.5%. FY2027 NOPAT therefore equals 51.2% of BFL attributable PAT (12,054 cr on the base path). The holdco discount is NOT in this rate; it is an explicit equity-bridge item.

scenario_narratives.base: Bajaj Finance keeps compounding but decelerates: NII growth 24% in FY2027 (H1 FY2027 ran +26%) tapering to 8% by FY2036, PBT/NII steady near 58.5% as FY2026's elevated credit costs (captive 2/3-wheeler and unsecured MSME) normalise against opex leverage from AI-led cost ratios, and the 21% CRAR is gradually levered toward ~17.5% so FCFE rises from ~2% of NII to ~30% by the terminal year. The insurers are worth what Allianz sold them for in March 2025 (53,000 cr general, 40,000 cr life); the emerging businesses are worth their book; and BFS shareholders receive 80 cents per rupee of look-through value on the BFL stake and insurers -- a 20% holdco discount in line with the sell-side convention for this name and narrower than today's ~28% market-implied discount to parts-at-market.
scenario_narratives.bull: India's retail-credit runway (management cites a $3.2tn opportunity by FY2030) lets BFL hold its 25-27% long-range AUM ambition for three more years with credit costs falling back toward 1.5%, lifting PBT/NII to 61%; excess capital is actively levered (CRAR to ~16%) so FCFE expands faster; and group simplification after the Allianz exit (BFS now consolidates 75% of both insurers with full strategic control, 100% FDI opens strategic options) narrows the holdco discount (the fixed bridge item is ~15% of this scenario's look-through value). Terminal growth 6.5% in INR.
scenario_narratives.bear: The unsecured consumer and MSME cycle that produced the Q2 FY2026 GNPA uptick deepens and RBI re-tightens risk weights or product permissions (as in 2023-24): BFL growth halves to 15% then 5-8%, PBT/NII falls to 52% for two years on 2.5%+ credit costs, no capital is released (CRAR stays ~21%), and the holdco layer -- BFS reinvesting BFL dividends in sub-scale Health/Direct/AMC ventures while promoter entities, not BFS, took the Allianz stakes -- is marked by the market at a ~30% discount (the fixed bridge item is ~30% of this scenario's look-through value). Insurers held at the deal anchors (no scenario variation in the bridge). Terminal growth 5.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; moved to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because BFS is a single-subsidiary concentration (Bajaj Finance is ~75-80% of value) sitting on a 10-quarter-high GNPA with guidance already cut once, plus a second-layer capital-allocation risk at the holdco. Bull cut to 25% because it needs three independent things: BFL re-accelerating with falling credit costs, active capital release, and a narrowing holdco discount.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Bajaj Finserv is valued as the sum of its parts because it is a holding company whose consolidated cash flow is dominated by Bajaj Finance's loan growth (structurally negative OCF) and whose consolidated profit is after a ~49% minority. The dominant part, the 51.2% stake in listed Bajaj Finance, is valued on its own economics -- FCFE (PAT less the equity retained to fund growth) discounted at a 12.5% INR cost of equity -- rather than marked at a market price of 29x earnings and 5.4x book. The two insurers are anchored on the arm's-length price Allianz accepted in March 2025, which is the best observable value for unlisted 75% stakes. A holdco discount of 20% of base-case look-through value (effectively ~30% in the bear case and ~15% in the bull) recognises that minority holders of BFS can only realise value at a market price that has carried a 15-35% discount to parts for a decade, and that BFS reinvests subsidiary dividends into loss-making incubations. House and street bases coincide (SBC is expensed inside subsidiary PAT, no second charge).
key_risks_to_valuation: Bajaj Finance is ~75-80% of value: a 1pp change in its sustained NII growth or a 1pp change in cost of equity moves BFS's value by double digits; the market currently prices BFL at a cost of equity nearer 10-11% than the 12.5% used here.
Asset quality in unsecured consumer and MSME lending (GNPA 1.24% Q2 FY2026, credit cost guided 1.85-1.95%) and RBI regulatory action (2023 risk-weight hike, 2023-24 eCOM/Insta EMI card embargo).
Holdco discount is a judgment (20% of base look-through value, fixed in INR across scenarios); the market-implied discount to parts-at-market was 27.8% on 6 Nov 2026 and has ranged 15-35%.
Insurer values rest on a single March-2025 transaction (1.58x embedded value for life, 29x PAT for general) and do not vary by scenario; +/-20% on them is ~+/-INR 69/share.
Loss of Allianz's reinsurance and actuarial support after the JV exit; renamed Bajaj General and Bajaj Life must sustain underwriting discipline alone.
Equity-retention assumption: the base case assumes BFL's CRAR drifts from 21% toward 17.5%; if management keeps CRAR at ~21% through the horizon, FCFE is lower (see bear capex path).
Anchor vintage: BFS standalone surplus, insurer net worth/EV are 30 Sep 2025 (latest filing in corpus); FY2026 AR and H1 FY2027 deck should be extracted and this build refreshed.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NSE regular close); 52-week range 1,597.0-2,126.8. Bajaj Finance and Bajaj Housing Finance prices from the same endpoint at the same close.
data_sources.financials: BAJAJFINSV.NS_Metrics.csv (FY2014-FY2025 consolidated, Ind AS from FY2018); FY2025 Annual Report (Tables 11 and 13: standalone financials, segment PAT; pp.5137-5160 Allianz SPA terms and 75.01% outcome); H1 FY2026 investor presentation (30 Sep 2025 performance summary, group structure 51.32%/74%, capital adequacy table, BALIC EV walk, BAGIC net worth); stockanalysis.com for Bajaj Finance and Bajaj Finserv FY2026 annual and TTM-to-Sep-2026 income statement, balance sheet and share counts (the FY2026 AR and H1 FY2027 results are not yet in Extracted/).
data_sources.qualitative: BAJAJFINSV.NS_Analysis.json (2026-11-08): business model, segment weights, guidance (BFL AUM 22-23%, credit cost 1.85-1.95%), bull/bear axes, Allianz buyout completion Jan-2026.

sotp.units: INR millions unless stated; per-share on 1,612m diluted shares

parts_at_market_cross_check.bajaj_finance_stake_note: 51.2% x 6,223m shares x INR 1,087.75 (NSE close 6 Nov 2026); BFL market cap INR 6,769,068m = 29.0x FY2026 attributable PAT 19,017 cr, 5.4x Sep-2026 book.

sotp.insurer_anchor_sensitivity: +/-20% on the two insurer anchors (after the 20% holdco discount) = +/- INR 111,615m = +/- INR 69/share.
sotp.allianz_transaction: SPAs 17 Mar 2025: Allianz's 26% in BAGIC for 13,780 cr and in BALIC for 10,400 cr (24,180 cr total). BFS acquires 1.01% of each (to 75.01%); promoter-group entities the remaining 24.99%. CCI and IRDAI approvals received 2025; entities renamed Bajaj General Insurance / Bajaj Life Insurance Oct 2025; first tranche completed Jan 2026 per Analysis.json; SPA long-stop 16 Oct 2026.

holdco_discount.method: 20% x base-case look-through value of (BFL stake stream EV 1,879,158m + insurer stakes 697,593m) = -515,350m = -INR 319.7/share, fixed across scenarios
